title: Can the attacker take the stage from a retreating Fox for free?
summary: Mid-stage the standoff holds: to 8 frames nothing forces the defender back, and walking in gains the attacker nothing. The attacker has a small edge only when the defender already stands at the ledge.
plan: For a grid of starting positions (attacker standing, walking in or dashing in; 15 distances; mid-stage and six distances from the ledge) find which defender inputs are safe for 8 frames against an attacker who sees each input first. Then solve the real one-frame-late game at the positions where none is safe.

details.label: Positions searched
details.value: about 1.4 billion (90 grid jobs, 6 exact solves)

details.label: Result
details.value: no way found from the middle of the stage to the ledge; the standoff stands at this depth

findings: Proven, 8 frames, mid-stage: attacker walking in at 13.9 against a standing Fox is worth exactly 0 (attacker's clean first hits minus defender's). Both wait.
Proven, 8 frames, mid-stage: both standing 12.1 apart is worth exactly 0. Both wait.

Proven, 8 frames, mid-stage: against an attacker who sees each input first, a Fox walking in at 13.5 to 14.1 leaves only steps away as safe inputs, but the step costs under 3 units, so the defender is not pushed back.
Proven, 8 frames, at the ledge, both standing 10.3 apart: 0 if falling off costs nothing, +0.27 for the attacker if leaving the stage loses the exchange.
Proven, 8 frames, at the ledge, attacker walking in at 13.9: +0.08 for the attacker with the same rule.
Not searched: more than 8 frames ahead, where a slower squeeze could still exist. Each extra frame about doubles the work.
